misconceptions.description: Treating all algorithmic bias as historical bias and ignoring representation, measurement, aggregation, evaluation, and feedback-loop sources
misconceptions.trigger: learner says 'the data is biased because the world is biased' as a complete diagnosis
misconceptions.feedback: Historical bias is one of six sources. Different sources demand different interventions. A diagnosis that names only history will misroute the fix.

misconceptions.description: Assuming a proxy variable measures what it is named to measure equally across groups
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses a proxy without checking subgroup correlation with the actual target
misconceptions.feedback: Measurement bias appears when the same underlying state produces different proxy values across groups. Always check that the proxy's correlation with the target holds in each subgroup, not just overall.

misconceptions.description: Believing additional data always reduces bias regardless of bias source
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes 'collect more data' as the universal fix
misconceptions.feedback: More data of the same kind does not fix historical, measurement, or feedback-loop bias. It often deepens them. Diagnose the source first; the right intervention may involve changing target, breaking the loop, or declining to deploy.

misconceptions.description: Believing post-processing 'debiasing' can fix any bias source
misconceptions.trigger: learner proposes post-hoc score adjustment as the answer to every bias case
misconceptions.feedback: Post-processing reshuffles errors. It cannot create missing information, rewrite the target variable, or break a feedback loop. Some biases are not engineering-fixable.
